activities.name: Travelling in the harmattan
activities.note: nothing closes; the harmattan is the dry season, and it is what makes the roads passable — the trade-off is the dust

windows.reason: the haziest weeks: dust off the Sahara cuts visibility sharply, and humidity drops far enough to be uncomfortable
the harmattan runs from late November to mid-March — dry, cool mornings and hazy skies, and the peak of the West African dry season

activities.name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
activities.note: far fewer birds, and in the rains the sanctuary shuts for about three months because moving about becomes impossible

windows.reason: the migration peak, with close to 400 bird species in the park
either side of the peak: the migration gets going in December and thins from late February

activities.name: Niokolo-Koba National Park
activities.note: in the rains (late June to late October) the animals disperse and the tracks need 4WD more than ever

windows.reason: dry season: the best game viewing, from the end of October to the end of June, when most tours run
five days of concerts on Saint-Louis's Place Baya, usually in May; dates are set each year
